scores.evidence: GitHub's merge API and pushes need `contents:write`, and workflow files need `workflows`, so the App structurally cannot merge.
scores.rationale: Mostly accurate on GitHub App permissions, webhook timeout, fork PR secrets and pull_request_target. A few imprecisions remain: 'contents:read only' versus pushing to a fork, and the approver permission check.

scores.evidence: I assume draft PRs that humans review and merge; the agent never merges or closes an issue on its own.
scores.rationale: Resolves the ambiguity of 'resolve' sensibly, covers triage and fix, is buildable in phases, and gives explicit deferrals with pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: The tool executor holds short-lived installation tokens; the model never sees them.
scores.rationale: Responsibilities, data ownership (GitHub as record, Postgres as ledger) and the trust boundary are applied consistently. Minor loose ends: a stated 'autonomous' comment tier versus fork ownership, and the 'close' approval versus the §1 claim that the agent never closes.

scores.evidence: ≥ 200 CI cases across issue body, comments, repo files, tool/test output... honeytokens planted; forged, replayed and edited approvals; a 2-day security-team red team
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, the riskiest parts are checked early, there are post-cutoff eval sets, thresholds are labeled as assumptions, and production monitoring continues through breakers and wave gates.

scores.evidence: Throughput | — | UNKNOWN: issue and comment event rate per target repo. Phase 0 measures it
scores.rationale: Figures are labeled REQUIREMENT, ASSUMPTION, UNKNOWN or BASELINE. Missing inputs are listed with what changes if they are wrong and how they will be confirmed.

scores.evidence: Agent output is stripped of external URLs and images, which closes exfiltration through rendered markdown.
scores.rationale: Covers injection, exfiltration, forged approvals, missed webhooks, label-triggered automation, pull_request_target, test tampering, cost spam, poisoning of feedback and sandbox escape, with concrete handling and recovery.

scores.evidence: One rollback is done by redeploying the previous image digest. A global write kill-switch flag exists from day zero.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, alerts, per-phase rollback and ownership (one team, business-hours on-call) are covered. Incident response detail and on-call runbooks are thin.

scores.evidence: Per-run hard caps | Triage: 30k tokens. Fix attempt: $5, 60 tool calls, 45 min | ASSUMPTION
scores.rationale: Covers per-run, per-author and monthly caps, the breaker and cost per merged PR against human cost. Lacks an aggregate run-cost estimate and build-cost or people-cost reasoning.

scores.evidence: R3: a merged backdoor or leaked secret cannot be undone
scores.rationale: Each decision carries a reversibility grade, validation and revisit trigger. The one-way decisions are concentrated on and isolated behind interfaces, with fallbacks named.

scores.evidence: One service (webhook receiver + workers), a managed queue, Postgres, a sandbox pool; one team, on call in business hours
scores.rationale: Starts simple, with one deployable and deferral of many features. The heavy process (seven V-checks, a 2-day red team, a 2-week hold per wave) and the gVisor/Firecracker sandbox are somewhat heavy but justified by the risk.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: a team member opens an issue on `org/agent-sandbox`... applies exactly one label from `{bug, feature, question}`, and the run ID is recorded.
scores.rationale: A concrete thin end-to-end slice, dependency-ordered phases, checkable exit criteria and fallbacks if checks fail make the plan directly startable.

checklist.evidence: Autonomous: read; apply allowed labels; comment... Needs bound human approval: close, assign, start a fix attempt. Never: merge, push upstream, edit `.github/` or secrets
Upstream permissions: `issues:write`, `pull_requests:write`, `contents:read` only. Code goes to a fork the agent owns
No filter stops every injection, so containment must be built into the structure
A fresh gVisor/Firecracker sandbox for each attempt: no credentials, outbound traffic only to a package mirror, destroyed by a time-to-live reaper
Replay ≥ 100 closed issues... scored by the real fix's tests hidden from the agent; A diff guard that flags deleted, skipped or weakened tests
≥ 300 issues created after the training cutoff... duplicate precision ≥ 0.90
A quality circuit breaker per repo: auto-pause when the correction rate rises above that repo's Phase 2 level.
A forced runaway loop is cut off at its cap and emits a cost metric. A global write kill-switch flag exists from day zero.
cost per merged PR below the human cost per fix
Decision log for every allowed or denied tool call, with the reason; Postgres action ledger
Prompts plus retrieval (issue index, code search, CODEOWNERS)
Idempotency on the delivery ID; A reconciliation sweep that re-lists issues since the last checkpoint; An attempt starts only on a maintainer trigger bound to the issue and commit.

traps.evidence: Merging stays behind branch protection and a human CODEOWNERS review. The App also has no `contents:write`.
Sandbox with no credentials and an outbound allow-list; the model never sees tokens
All issue, comment, repo and tool text is treated as data. The executor allow-list and permission design limit the damage when an injection works
≥ 50% of opened PRs merged with only minor edits; cost per merged PR below the human cost per fix
Fix attempt: $5, 60 tool calls, 45 min; a monthly circuit breaker

note: Very strong, security-first plan with explicit assumptions, risk-targeted validation and reversibility grading. Weak spots: thin incident response and run-cost quantification, plus somewhat heavy process.
